newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Distillers 1996 pre-tax profit rises 7.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Irish Distillers 1996 pre-tax profit rises 7.0 pct.

text.p: Irish Distillers, a subsidiary of French group Pernod Ricard, said on Thursday that profits before tax and exceptional items rose by seven percent to 49.2 million Irish pounds IN 1996.
The company, which distills, blends and distributes spirts and wines and also distributes foods, said turnover rose by 8.8 percent to 616 million Irish pounds.
Irish Distillers' main whisky brand, Jameson, had an exceptional year, growing world-wide by 17.6 percent and increasing its shipments to one million standard cases, the company said.
"A long-term target of two million cases has been set by Groupe Pernod Ricard for Jameson," Irish Distillers said.
The company's other whisky brands also performed well with sales of Power's Gold Label growing by six percent, Paddy whisky up by five percent while Bushmills advanced by 0.6 percent.
Total sales of branded products in 1996 amounted to 3.4 million standard cases, an increase of 12.5 percent on 1995.
Geographically, Irish Distillers' products recorded growth of 5.7 percent in the Republic of Ireland, reflecting the strength of domestic economic growth.

Other markets that performed well included Britain, where the company saw growth of 13 percent, France, where Irish Distillers recorded growth of 47 percent, and Australia/South Africa, up 30 percent.
Shipments to the North American markets remained constant, Irish Distillers said.
The company said its food and drink distribution division, BWG Ltd, enjoyed strong growth in sales and profits last year.
BWG operates the SPAR convenience store franchise in the Republic of Ireland, MACE in Northern Ireland and cash and carry outlets.
